## Introduction

We will store versions of the
documented dataset and retrieve a model by its
identifier. By the end, you should be able to explain how a version
identifier links a result to the exact input that produced it.

## Store dataset versions with pins

A *pins* board stores named objects (which is usually files), called
pins. We use a local folder board to save our pins.

We will write two versions of the `health_wellbeing` pin.
The first contains all 29 studies, with the data source and hash as metadata. The second contains the 18 general-population studies.  

```{r health-versioning-board-load-data, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
source("pipelines/workshop_support.R")
use_workshop_book_outputs()

box::use(
  pins[board_folder, pin_exists, pin_meta, pin_read, pin_versions, board_temp, pin_write],
  utils[read.csv],
  vetiver[vetiver_model, vetiver_pin_write, vetiver_pin_read]
)

raw_file <- file.path("data", "raw", "healthwellbeing.rda")
source_url <- paste0(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MathiasHarrer/dmetar/",
  "38c9b9bb5f85ea49de33e5d2536f6544d5268517/data/HealthWellbeing.rda"
)

dir.create(dirname(raw_file), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
if (!file.exists(raw_file)) {
  download.file(source_url, destfile = raw_file, mode = "wb")
}

load(raw_file)
all_df <- HealthWellbeing
general_df <- HealthWellbeing |>
  subset(population == "general population")

head(general_df, 8)
```
We next create 2 pins for each version of the dataset:

```{r save-health-versioning-board-write, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
board <- board_temp(versioned = TRUE)
pin_write(
  board,
  all_df,
  name = "health_wellbeing",
  type = "rds",
  title = "HealthWellbeing",
  description = "All 29 studies in the teaching snapshot.",
  metadata = list(
    scope = "all",
    filter = "all studies"
  )
)

pin_write(
  board,
  general_df,
  name = "health_wellbeing",
  type = "rds",
  title = "HealthWellbeing",
  description = "Only studies labelled general population.",
  metadata = list(
    scope = "general",
    filter = "population == 'general population'"
  )
)
```

We open the same board and list its versions.

```{r health-versioning-board, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
source("pipelines/prepare_versioning_demo.R")

workshop_dir <- workshop_output_dir()
data_board <- board_folder(
  file.path(workshop_dir, "data_store"),
  versioned = TRUE
)
pin_versions(data_board, "health_wellbeing")
```

The script also recorded which identifier belongs to which dataset (the `version` column).
We retrieve the subset's metadata and the full dataset by those
identifiers.

```{r health-versioning-read-full, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
versions <- read.csv(
  file.path(workshop_dir, "dataset-versions.csv"),
  colClasses = "character"
)
full_version <- versions$version[versions$scope == "all"]
general_version <- versions$version[versions$scope == "general"]

pin_meta(data_board, "health_wellbeing", version = full_version)$user[
  c("scope", "filter", "source_url")
]
```

We will also view the filtered dataset.

```{r health-versioning-read-general, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
pin_meta(data_board, "health_wellbeing", version = general_version)$user[
  c("scope", "filter", "parent_version", "source_url")
]
```

A version identifier names a stored object within this board. It is read from the exact full version, and its metadata
records the filter and that parent version. 

## Store model versions with vetiver

We have assessed whether our dataset adheres to FAIR principles and we have also versioned it. We can next do some statistical modelling. Typically, we might want to use a mixed-effects model to perform a meta-analysis, but for the purposes of this demonstration we shall fit a linear regression model of Fisher z (`atanh(cor)`) against log sample
size, then store it with *vetiver*.  

We will first process the data.

```{r health-original-processing, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
health_full <- pin_read(
  data_board, "health_wellbeing", version = full_version
)

original <- data.frame(
  population = factor(health_full$population),
  z = atanh(health_full$cor),
  log_n = log(health_full$n)
)
head(original, 5)
```

Subsequently, we fit and save a linear regression.

```{r health-original-lm-pin-write, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
lm_model <- stats::lm(z ~ log_n, data = original)

v_model <- vetiver_model(lm_model, model_name = "health_wellbeing_lm")
vetiver_pin_write(board, v_model)
```

We will next reload the model from a `vetiver` pin. Its input prototype lists the columns required for prediction. Its
metadata records the training data version and hash.

```{r health-vetiver-read, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, eval = TRUE}
version_file <- file.path(workshop_dir, "predictive-model-version.txt")
model_version <- readLines(version_file, warn = FALSE)
model_board <- pins::board_folder(file.path(workshop_dir, "model_store"), versioned = TRUE)
model_lm <- vetiver::vetiver_pin_read(
  model_board, "health_wellbeing_lm", version = model_version
)
tibble::tibble(
  name = model_lm$model_name,
  description = model_lm$description,
  version = model_lm$metadata$version,
  recipe = model_lm$metadata$user$recipe,
  r_version = model_lm$metadata$user$r_version,
  vetiver_version = model_lm$metadata$user$vetiver_version
)
```

We can save and reload both data and models, which we treat as a versioned artifacts with their respective metadata.
